page: Hetzner Cloud ccx53 is a dedicated CPU instance featuring 32 vCPUs and 16 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this virtualized server utilizes the QEMU hypervisor. It is equipped with 125.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.91 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a 600 GB local NVMe SSD, and there are no integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded bzip3 decompression placing in the top 25%. The server also demonstrates strong cryptographic execution, as shown by its PassMark CPU encryption score, and strong memory performance with a high PassMark memory score. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average tier. For language model workloads, the instance achieves top-tier text generation speeds with small 135M models, but drops to poor performance when generating text with large 70B models.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ccx53 offers a resource-dense profile suitable for workloads requiring consistent CPU performance without virtualization overhead. The inclusion of local NVMe storage supports database operations and static web serving, both of which perform at average tier levels. This server is suited for general-purpose enterprise applications, medium-scale databases, software compilation, and lightweight machine learning inference, though it is not designed for large-scale LLM execution or GPU-dependent tasks.
